name: Notion API (public connections)
verdict: Create a public connection with installation scope 'Any workspace' in the Notion Developer portal. That one setting cannot be changed later. Any Notion user can authorize it right away with no app review; Marketplace listing is optional, takes 5–10 business days, and is reviewed by Notion.

difficulty.label: Easy
difficulty.rationale: Fully self-serve: no security assessment, no verification queue, and no user cap for OAuth. The only review is optional Marketplace listing. The main complexity is the page-picker access model, and recent token-model changes (per-authorization tokens with refresh tokens).

first_token.note: Developer portal > Build > Public connections > Create new connection. Fill in the name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope and capabilities, copy the OAuth client ID and secret from the Configuration tab, and run the code flow.

production.estimate: Same day without a Marketplace listing; 1–3 weeks with one
production.active_effort: 2–4 hours (organization info, privacy policy, listing assets)
production.waiting: None for OAuth use. Marketplace listing review: Notion replies within 5–10 business days.
production.note: No approval gate for OAuth. The time goes into correct capability selection, handling page-picker UX (users must share pages), and, optionally, Marketplace review.

paths.name: Internal connection (static token)
paths.who_for: Agents operating on your own workspace only
paths.limits: One workspace. You must be a workspace owner to create it. Pages must be shared with the connection manually (••• > Connections). No OAuth.

paths.name: Public connection, 'Selected workspaces only'
paths.who_for: Pilots or a fixed set of customer workspaces
paths.limits: Only the workspaces chosen at creation can install it. Not Marketplace eligible. Scope cannot be changed after creation.

paths.name: Public connection, 'Any workspace'
paths.review: none for OAuth. Optional Notion review for a Marketplace listing.
paths.limits: Each user authorizes individually and only sees pages they shared through the page picker. Marketplace-eligible.

prerequisites.item: Notion account and a development workspace
Organization information: company name, website, privacy policy URL (and terms/support email if prompted)
prerequisites.note: Third-party setup guides report these as required fields in the public connection form.

prerequisites.item: HTTPS redirect URI(s) on your backend
Listing name, description, category/tags, logo and images (only for a Marketplace listing)

steps.title: Create the public connection
steps.detail: Developer portal > Build > Public connections > Create new connection. Enter the Connection name, Development workspace, Redirect URI(s), and Installation scope: choose 'Any workspace' for a multi-tenant product, because it is set once and is permanent. Fill in the organization fields (company name, website, privacy policy).

steps.title: Select capabilities
steps.detail: Choose only what the agent needs: Read content, Update content, Insert content, comment read/insert, and user information (with or without email). Users see these on the consent screen.

steps.title: Copy credentials
steps.detail: Configuration tab > OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret. Store the secret server-side. The token endpoint uses HTTP Basic auth with base64(client_id:client_secret).

steps.title: Optional: template URL
steps.detail: Set 'Notion URL for optional template' so users can duplicate a starter page during authorization. The token response then includes duplicated_template_id.

steps.title: Run the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&response_type=code&owner=user&redirect_uri=...&state=.... The user picks pages in the page picker. POST https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code, code, and redirect_uri (required if it was sent in the authorize URL or if the connection has more than one URI). Store access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, workspace_id and owner. Include the Notion-Version header on API calls.

steps.title: Implement refresh and the empty-access state
steps.detail: Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token at the same token endpoint. A new refresh token is returned each time, so persist it atomically and serialize concurrent refreshes. If search returns nothing, guide the user to re-open the page picker or share pages with the connection.

steps.title: Optional: submit a Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Developer portal > Listings > create a listing (name, description, category, tags, logo, images) linked to the public connection, then submit. Track status under Listings > Connections.

review.trigger: Only when you submit a Marketplace listing (requires installation scope 'Any workspace'). OAuth installs need no review.
review.process: Submit the listing in Developer portal > Listings. The Notion team reviews every submission and emails approval or feedback. Revise and resubmit if needed.
reviewers_check: Brand and trademark use (no implying a Notion partnership)
Baseline connection criteria in Notion's Connection Gallery best practices
common_rejections: Quality concerns with the listing or connection
Connection created with 'Selected workspaces only' scope, which is ineligible and must be recreated

pre_approval_limits: None for OAuth. Any Notion user can authorize an 'Any workspace' public connection immediately
'Selected workspaces only' connections are limited to the workspaces chosen at creation
API rate limit (about 3 requests/second average per connection) applies regardless of review

oauth.refresh_tokens: Yes. The token response includes refresh_token (nullable in the schema). Refreshing with grant_type=refresh_token returns a new access token and a new refresh token. Community reports say the old refresh token stops working (rotation), and reusing it gives invalid_grant. Since June 8, 2026, new public connections issue a unique token pair per authorization, including re-authorizations.
oauth.access_token_lifetime: Not documented. The token response has no expires_in field. Community sources say tokens expire, so refresh on 401 and proactively.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Registered in the Developer portal when creating the connection, and multiple URIs are allowed. redirect_uri in the token request is required if it was in the authorize URL or if the connection has more than one URI, and is not allowed otherwise. HTTPS, wildcard and localhost rules are not documented. Use exact HTTPS URIs.
oauth.scopes: No OAuth scope strings. Access is governed by capabilities chosen on the connection (read/update/insert content, comments, user info with or without email), plus page-level access chosen by each user in the page picker. Sharing a parent page grants its children.
oauth.tenant_notes: Tokens are per user per workspace authorization (owner=user), identified by bot_id. Key storage by bot_id, not workspace_id, because multiple users in one workspace each get their own token. A connection only sees pages the authorizing user has full access to and shared. Workspace admins can restrict which connections members may add.

gotchas.title: Installation scope is permanent
gotchas.detail: 'Any workspace' vs 'Selected workspaces only' is set at creation and cannot be changed. Only 'Any workspace' is Marketplace-eligible. Choosing wrong means a new connection with new client credentials, and all users must reconnect.

gotchas.title: Users pick pages, so the agent may see nothing
gotchas.detail: The page picker shows only pages the user has full access to, and only selected pages (and their children) are shared. If the user clicks Allow but does not finish the flow, or skips selection, the connection has no access. Build an empty-state that sends them back to the picker.

gotchas.title: Refresh tokens rotate: serialize refreshes
gotchas.detail: Each refresh returns a new refresh token. Concurrent agent workers refreshing the same connection will invalidate each other and get invalid_grant, which requires the user to re-authorize.

gotchas.title: One token per user per authorization, keyed by bot_id
gotchas.detail: Tokens are user-level and, since June 2026, each authorization (even a re-authorization) yields a new token pair for new connections. Keying storage by workspace_id overwrites other users' tokens.

gotchas.title: Naming changed: 'integrations' became 'connections'
gotchas.detail: Current docs say internal and public 'connections' and the 'Developer portal' (launched May 12, 2026). Older tutorials say 'integrations' and notion.so/my-integrations. Personal access tokens are a third option for single-user scripts.

gotchas.title: Token lifetime undocumented
gotchas.detail: The official token schema has no expires_in, but refresh tokens exist and community sources say access tokens expire. Implement refresh-on-401 rather than assuming tokens never expire (the pre-2025 behavior).

blockers.cause: User cancelled the consent or page picker
blockers.fix: Show a retry button. Explain that page selection is required.

blockers.symptom: API returns object_not_found / empty search results after a successful OAuth
blockers.cause: The page was not shared with the connection in the picker
blockers.fix: Ask the user to re-run authorization and select pages, or use ••• > Connections on the page to add your connection.

blockers.cause: Reused a rotated refresh token, the user disconnected the connection, or a redirect_uri/credential mismatch
blockers.fix: Store the latest refresh token atomically, lock refreshes per bot_id, and if it persists prompt the user to reconnect.

blockers.symptom: invalid_request / redirect_uri errors on token exchange
blockers.cause: redirect_uri sent when not allowed, or omitted when required (multiple URIs configured)
blockers.fix: Send redirect_uri in the token request exactly when you sent it in the authorize URL or when more than one URI is registered.

blockers.symptom: Need Marketplace listing but connection is 'Selected workspaces only'
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with 'Any workspace' and migrate users.

agent_can: Generate redirect URIs and the authorize URL
Implement the token exchange with Basic auth, refresh with locking, and bot_id-keyed storage
Draft the privacy policy and listing copy
Create the optional template page content
human_must: Sign in to Notion and create the connection in the Developer portal
Upload the logo and listing images
Submit the Marketplace listing and respond to feedback

probes.result: Redirects to Notion login; client validated after sign-in
probes.method: Live browser request (no account created, no credentials used)
